country.name: Denmark
country.tagline: Solaris, sea air and long summer light: a twenty-first-century wine country on the edge of the map.

stats.note: About 173 ha and 146 vineyards in 2022 (Wikipedia, Danish wine).

country.overview:
Danish monasteries made a little wine for their own use from the thirteenth century, but commercial wine-growing only became legal in 1999, when a ban was lifted and 99 hectares were allowed for wine grapes; the 2001 vintage was the first sold. Since then the number of vineyards has grown from about 20 in 2006 to 146 in 2022, on about 173 hectares, most of them on Zealand and Bornholm.

The climate is cool, but long summer days at 55 to 57 degrees north, a sunny Baltic microclimate and warming summers let early-ripening, mostly fungus-resistant grapes succeed: Solaris above all, plus Rondo, Regent, Cabernet Cortis, Souvignier Gris and some Pinot Noir and Chardonnay for sparkling. Skærsøgaard at Dons near Kolding pioneered quality sparkling wine, and its Dons became Denmark's first PDO in 2018. Regional designations exist for Fyn, Jylland, Sjælland and Bornholm. Denmark also has a thriving fruit-wine and cider culture, and Frederiksdal on Lolland is famous for its cherry wine.

history.title: Monastic wine
history.text: Monasteries made small amounts of wine for their own use; it was never commercial.

history.title: Wine-growing becomes legal
history.text: A ban on commercial wine-growing was lifted in 1999 after EU recognition; the 2001 vintage was the first sold legally.

history.title: Dons PDO
history.text: Dons near Kolding, home of Skærsøgaard, was registered as Denmark's first PDO, for quality sparkling wine.

country.classification: One PDO, Dons (2018, quality sparkling wine from Kolding municipality). The Danish authority publishes product specifications for the regional designations Fyn, Jylland and Sjælland (still, sparkling and quality sparkling, max. 60 hl/ha) and Bornholm; these regional names are commonly described as PGIs, but the specifications themselves only say 'protected designation', so their exact status should be confirmed in eAmbrosia.
country.climate_soils: Cool maritime with long summer days. Bornholm's granite and Baltic sunshine make it one of the warmest parts of Denmark; elsewhere vines grow on glacial moraine, clay and sand.

grapes.name: Solaris
grapes.note: The dominant white, ripening early with good sugar.

grapes.name: Cabernet Cortis, Souvignier Gris, Muscaris, Orion
Pinot Noir, Chardonnay
grapes.note: For sparkling wine at Dons and elsewhere.

further_reading: Fødevarestyrelsen product specifications for Danish wine designations

regions.name: Denmark
regions.tagline: Vineyards on Jutland, Funen, Zealand and Bornholm.
regions.summary: Danish vineyards are scattered across the country, with the largest concentration on Zealand (especially North Zealand) and Bornholm, plus Funen and Jutland. Dons near Kolding in south-east Jutland has the only PDO.
regions.history: Legal commercial wine-growing dates only from 1999.
regions.terroir: Moraine, clay, sand; granite on Bornholm.
regions.grapes: Solaris, Rondo, Regent, Cabernet Cortis, Souvignier Gris, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay.
regions.styles: Dry whites, sparkling, rosé, light reds, fruit wines.
regions.classification: PDO Dons; regional designations Fyn, Jylland, Sjælland, Bornholm.

dk-bornholm.name: Bornholm
dk-bornholm.summary: The Baltic island of Bornholm has granite soils and the sunniest climate in Denmark, and several vineyards, including Lille Gadegård at Pedersker. Its designation status should be confirmed in eAmbrosia.
dk-bornholm.terroir: Granite and sandstone; sunny Baltic microclimate.

dk-dons.name: Dons
dk-dons.grapes: Solaris, Madeleine Angevine, Orion, Zalas Perle, Pinot Noir, Rondo, Regent, Cabernet Cortis
dk-dons.summary: Dons, in Kolding municipality in south-east Jutland, became Denmark's first PDO in 2018, and the first protected appellation for sparkling wine in Northern Europe. It exists because of Skærsøgaard, where Sven Moesgaard planted vines in 1998 and began making traditional-method sparkling wine; the estate's Dons Cuvée won international medals from the 2006 vintage on. Rules are strict: a maximum yield of 30 hl/ha and quality sparkling wine only.
dk-dons.terroir: Glacial moraine around the lakes of Dons in south-east Jutland.
dk-dons.nerd_note: The EU register caps Dons yields at 5,000 kg of grapes per hectare, among the lowest of any PDO in Europe.

dk-fyn.name: Fyn
dk-fyn.grapes: Solaris, Rondo, Regent, Pinot Noir and other permitted varieties
dk-fyn.summary: The regional designation for wine from Funen and its surrounding islands, covering still, sparkling and quality sparkling wine with yields up to 60 hl/ha. Its status (PGI-level) should be confirmed in eAmbrosia.

dk-jylland.name: Jylland
dk-jylland.grapes: Solaris, Rondo, Regent, Pinot Noir and other permitted varieties
dk-jylland.summary: The regional designation for Jutland (the Midtjylland, Nordjylland and Syddanmark regions, excluding Funen), for still and sparkling wine with yields up to 60 hl/ha.

dk-sjaelland.name: Sjælland
dk-sjaelland.summary: The regional designation for Zealand and nearby islands, where most Danish vineyards are, notably in North Zealand and on the Røsnæs peninsula, home of Dyrehøj Vingaard.

sites.name: Skærsøgaard
sites.text: Sven Moesgaard's estate at Dons near Kolding, planted in 1998, whose sparkling wines led to Denmark's first PDO.

sites.name: Dyrehøj Vingaard
sites.text: A vineyard on the Røsnæs peninsula near Kalundborg, one of Denmark's largest and best known.

sites.name: Lille Gadegård
sites.text: A Bornholm farm estate near Pedersker that makes wine, cider and spirits in the island's sunny climate.
